Cardinal.commSemiring.fullDefinition: instance commSemiring : CommSemiring Cardinal.{u} where   zero := 0   one := 1   add := (· + ·)   mul := (· * ·)   zero_add a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_congr <| Equiv.emptySum (ULift (Fin 0)) α   add_zero a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_congr <| Equiv.sumEmpty α (ULift (Fin 0))   add_assoc a b c := inductionOn₃ a b c fun α β γ => mk_congr <| Equiv.sumAssoc α β γ   add_comm a b := inductionOn₂ a b fun α β => mk_congr <| Equiv.sumComm α β   zero_mul a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_eq_zero _   mul_zero a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_eq_zero _   one_mul a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_congr <| Equiv.uniqueProd α (ULift (Fin 1))   mul_one a := inductionOn a fun α => mk_congr <| Equiv.prodUnique α (ULift (Fin 1))   mul_assoc a b c := inductionOn₃ a b c fun α β γ => mk_congr <| Equiv.prodAssoc α β γ   mul_comm := mul_comm'   left_distrib a b c := inductionOn₃ a b c fun α β γ => mk_congr <| Equiv.prodSumDistrib α β γ   right_distrib a b c := inductionOn₃ a b c fun α β γ => mk_congr <| Equiv.sumProdDistrib α β γ   nsmul := nsmulRec   npow n c := c ^ (n : Cardinal)   npow_zero := @power_zero   npow_succ n c := show c ^ (↑(n + 1) : Cardinal) = c ^ (↑n : Cardinal) * c     by rw [Cardinal.cast_succ, power_add, power_one, mul_comm']   natCast := (fun n => lift.{u} #(Fin n) : ℕ → Cardinal.{u})   natCast_zero := rfl   natCast_succ := Cardinal.cast_succ

Cardinal.ofENat_le_ofENat.description: This shows that the less-than-or-equal relationship between extended natural numbers is maintained when they are converted into cardinals.

Cardinal.ofENat_le_nat.description: This demonstrates that the less-than-or-equal relationship between an extended natural number and a natural number is preserved when converted to their respective cardinal values.

explanatories.Function.Injective: This definition specifies a property of a function that ensures distinct inputs are mapped to distinct outputs.

Cardinal.ofENat_injective.description: This asserts that the transformation from extended natural numbers to cardinal values is an injective function.

Cardinal.ofENat_eq_nat.description: This establishes an equivalence between the equality of an extended natural number and a natural number when both are expressed as cardinals.

Cardinal.nat_eq_ofENat.description: This reveals an equivalence between the equality of a natural number and an extended natural number when both are represented as cardinals.

Cardinal.lift_ofENat.description: This shows that lifting the cardinal value of an extended natural number results in the same cardinal value.

Cardinal.ofENat_le_aleph0.description: This shows that any extended natural number, when transformed into a cardinal, is less than or equal to the cardinality of the smallest infinite set.

explanatories.Cardinal.ofENat: This establishes a transformation that converts extended natural numbers into cardinals, mapping natural numbers to themselves and infinity to the smallest infinite cardinal.

explanatories.Function.extend: The extension of a function defines a new mapping that combines the behavior of a given function with a secondary function to handle outputs outside the range of the first, ensuring that the resulting mapping is coherent under certain conditions.

Cardinal.toENatAux_eq_top.description: This states that if a cardinal number is at least countably infinite, its transformation to extended natural numbers results in the maximum value in that system.

Cardinal.toENatAux_zero.description: This asserts that the conversion of zero from a cardinal to an extended natural number results in zero.

Cardinal.toENatAux_ofENat.description: This demonstrates that converting an extended natural number to its corresponding extended natural value through a specific auxiliary function yields the same number.

Cardinal.toENatAux_gc.description: This establishes a Galois connection between the transformations of extended natural numbers and the auxiliary transformations of cardinals.

Cardinal.ofENat_nat.description: This states that when a natural number is represented as a cardinal, its double elevation equals its single elevation.

Cardinal.toENatAux_eq_nat.description: This demonstrates that the equality of the conversion of a cardinal to an extended natural number corresponds precisely to the equality of the cardinal and the extended natural number itself.

Cardinal.toENatAux_eq_zero.description: This establishes that a cardinal is zero if and only if its auxiliary extended natural number representation is also zero.

Cardinal.toENat.comment:
Projection from cardinals to `ℕ∞`. Sends all infinite cardinals to `⊤`.

We define this function as a bundled monotone ring homomorphism.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

explanatories.Cardinal.toENatAux: This defines a function that converts a cardinal number into an extended natural number in an unbundled format.

explanatories.Or.inl: If a proposition is true, then it can be included in a disjunction, demonstrating how to inject it into the logical framework of 'or'.

explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Nat.cast_mul: This theorem states that the natural number multiplication operation is compatible with the operation of multiplication in a non-associative semiring when interpreted in that structure.
explanatories.eq_or_ne: This theorem states that for any two elements, they are either equal or not equal, establishing a binary relationship.
explanatories.Ne: The inequality between two elements is defined by the negation of their equality, asserting that they are distinct.
explanatories.Cardinal.toENatAux_eq_zero: This establishes that a cardinal is zero if and only if its auxiliary extended natural number representation is also zero.
explanatories.le_mul_of_one_le_of_le: This theorem asserts that if one quantity is greater than or equal to one and another quantity is less than or equal to a third, then the first quantity multiplied by the third will also be greater than or equal to the second quantity.

Cardinal.toENat.fullDefinition: noncomputable def toENat : Cardinal.{u} →+*o ℕ∞ where   toFun := toENatAux   map_one' := toENatAux_nat 1   map_mul' x y := by     wlog hle : x ≤ y; · rw [mul_comm, this y x (le_of_not_le hle), mul_comm]     cases lt_or_le y ℵ₀ with     | inl hy =>       lift x to ℕ using hle.trans_lt hy; lift y to ℕ using hy       simp only [← Nat.cast_mul, toENatAux_nat]     | inr hy =>       rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx       · simp       · simp only [toENatAux_eq_top hy]         rw [toENatAux_eq_top, ENat.mul_top]         · rwa [Ne, toENatAux_eq_zero]         · exact le_mul_of_one_le_of_le (one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 hx) hy   map_add' x y := by     wlog hle : x ≤ y; · rw [add_comm, this y x (le_of_not_le hle), add_comm]     cases lt_or_le y ℵ₀ with     | inl hy =>       lift x to ℕ using hle.trans_lt hy; lift y to ℕ using hy       simp only [← Nat.cast_add, toENatAux_nat]     | inr hy =>       simp only [toENatAux_eq_top hy, add_top]       exact toENatAux_eq_top <| le_add_left hy   map_zero' := toENatAux_zero   monotone' := toENatAux_gc.monotone_u

Cardinal.alephIdx.initialSeg.code: Cardinal.alephIdx.initialSeg.{u_1} : (fun x x_1 => x < x_1) ≼i fun x x_1 => x < x_1
Cardinal.alephIdx.initialSeg.comment:
The `aleph'` index function, which gives the ordinal index of a cardinal.
(The `aleph'` part is because unlike `aleph` this counts also the
finite stages. So `alephIdx n = n`, `alephIdx ω = ω`,
`alephIdx ℵ₁ = ω + 1` and so on.)
In this definition, we register additionally that this function is an initial segment,
i.e., it is order preserving and its range is an initial segment of the ordinals.
For the basic function version, see `alephIdx`.
For an upgraded version stating that the range is everything, see `AlephIdx.rel_iso`.

explanatories.Ordinal: This definition establishes the type of well-orders within a specific type classification, accounting for equivalence under order isomorphism.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.collapse: This definition specifies that an initial segment can be constructed by collapsing an order embedding into a well-ordered set to fill in any gaps.
explanatories.OrderEmbedding.ltEmbedding: This defines a way to relate the order relation of two preordered types through an order embedding, ensuring that the order is preserved.

Cardinal.alephIdx.relIso.comment:
The `aleph'` index function, which gives the ordinal index of a cardinal.
(The `aleph'` part is because unlike `aleph` this counts also the
finite stages. So `alephIdx n = n`, `alephIdx ℵ₀ = ω`,
`alephIdx ℵ₁ = ω + 1` and so on.)
In this version, we register additionally that this function is an order isomorphism
between cardinals and ordinals.
For the basic function version, see `alephIdx`.

Cardinal.beth.comment:
Beth numbers are defined so that `beth 0 = ℵ₀`, `beth (succ o) = 2 ^ (beth o)`, and when `o` is
a limit ordinal, `beth o` is the supremum of `beth o'` for `o' < o`.

Assuming the generalized continuum hypothesis, which is undecidable in ZFC, `beth o = aleph o` for
every `o`.

Ordinal.cof.comment:
Cofinality of an ordinal. This is the smallest cardinal of a
subset `S` of the ordinal which is unbounded, in the sense
`∀ a, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≤ b`. It is defined for all ordinals, but
`cof 0 = 0` and `cof (succ o) = 1`, so it is only really
interesting on limit ordinals (when it is an infinite cardinal).

Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence.code: Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence.{u} (a o : Ordinal.{u}) (f : (b : Ordinal.{u}) → b < o → Ordinal.{u}) : Prop
Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence.comment:
A fundamental sequence for `a` is an increasing sequence of length `o = cof a` that converges at
`a`. We provide `o` explicitly in order to avoid type rewrites.

Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence.fullDefinition: def IsFundamentalSequence (a o : Ordinal.{u}) (f : ∀ b < o, Ordinal.{u}) : Prop :=   o ≤ a.cof.ord ∧ (∀ {i j} (hi hj), i < j → f i hi < f j hj) ∧ blsub.{u, u} o f = a

PSet.Equiv.comment:
Two pre-sets are extensionally equivalent if every element of the first family is extensionally
equivalent to some element of the second family and vice-versa.
PSet.Equiv.fullDefinition: def Equiv : PSet → PSet → Prop   | ⟨_, A⟩, ⟨_, B⟩ => (∀ a, ∃ b, Equiv (A a) (B b)) ∧ (∀ b, ∃ a, Equiv (A a) (B b))
PSet.Equiv.description: This defines a relation where two pre-sets are considered equivalent if there is a mutual correspondence between their elements based on extensionally equivalent conditions.

ZFSet.small_toSet.fullDefinition: instance small_toSet (x : ZFSet.{u}) : Small.{u} x.toSet :=   Quotient.inductionOn x fun a => by     let f : a.Type → (mk a).toSet := fun i => ⟨mk <| a.Func i, func_mem a i⟩     suffices Function.Surjective f by exact small_of_surjective this     rintro ⟨y, hb⟩     induction y using Quotient.inductionOn     cases' hb with i h     exact ⟨i, Subtype.coe_injective (Quotient.sound h.symm)⟩

explanatories.Prod.Lex.left: If one element is related to another via a specified relation, then the pair consisting of that element and a second element is also related to another pair in a lexicographic order defined by those relations.

SetTheory.PGame.LF.comment:
The less or fuzzy relation on pre-games.

If `0 ⧏ x`, then Left can win `x` as the first player.
SetTheory.PGame.LF.fullDefinition: def LF (x y : PGame) : Prop :=   ¬y ≤ x
SetTheory.PGame.LF.description: This definition establishes a fuzzy relation on pre-games indicating that the first player can win the game if the current position is preferable to zero.

SetTheory.PGame.le.fullDefinition: instance le : LE PGame :=   ⟨Sym2.GameAdd.fix wf_isOption fun x y le =>       (∀ i, ¬le y (x.moveLeft i) (Sym2.GameAdd.snd_fst <| IsOption.moveLeft i)) ∧         ∀ j, ¬le (y.moveRight j) x (Sym2.GameAdd.fst_snd <| IsOption.moveRight j)⟩

SetTheory.PGame.le_iff_forall_lf.comment:
Definition of `x ≤ y` on pre-games, in terms of `⧏`.

The ordering here is chosen so that `And.left` refer to moves by Left, and `And.right` refer to
moves by Right.

SetTheory.PGame.le_def.code:
SetTheory.PGame.le_def.{u_1} {x y : PGame} :
  x ≤ y ↔
    (∀ (i : x.LeftMoves), (∃ i', x.moveLeft i ≤ y.moveLeft i') ∨ ∃ j, (x.moveLeft i).moveRight j ≤ y) ∧
      ∀ (j : y.RightMoves), (∃ i, x ≤ (y.moveRight j).moveLeft i) ∨ ∃ j', x.moveRight j' ≤ y.moveRight j
SetTheory.PGame.le_def.comment: The definition of `x ≤ y` on pre-games, in terms of `≤` two moves later.

SetTheory.PGame.lf_def.code:
SetTheory.PGame.lf_def.{u_1} {x y : PGame} :
  x ⧏ y ↔
    (∃ i,
        (∀ (i' : x.LeftMoves), x.moveLeft i' ⧏ y.moveLeft i) ∧
          ∀ (j : (y.moveLeft i).RightMoves), x ⧏ (y.moveLeft i).moveRight j) ∨
      ∃ j,
        (∀ (i : (x.moveRight j).LeftMoves), (x.moveRight j).moveLeft i ⧏ y) ∧
          ∀ (j' : y.RightMoves), x.moveRight j ⧏ y.moveRight j'

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.comment:
The fuzzy, confused, or incomparable relation on pre-games.

If `x ‖ 0`, then the first player can always win `x`.
SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.fullDefinition: def Fuzzy (x y : PGame) : Prop :=   x ⧏ y ∧ y ⧏ x
SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.description: This definition describes a relation indicating that two pre-games are fuzzy or incomparable when neither has a winning advantage over the other.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap.code: SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap.{u_1} {x y : PGame} : x ‖ y → y ‖ x
SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap.description: This theorem demonstrates that if two game structures are in a fuzzy relationship, then their relationship is symmetric, meaning swapping the order of the games retains the fuzzy relationship.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap_iff.code: SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap_iff.{u_1} {x y : PGame} : x ‖ y ↔ y ‖ x
SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.swap_iff.description: This theorem states that two games are considered fuzzy equivalent if and only if swapping their positions maintains that equivalence.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_irrefl.description: This theorem demonstrates that no game can be fuzzy related to itself, implying a form of strict separation between any game and itself in terms of its relational structure.

SetTheory.PGame.lf_iff_lt_or_fuzzy.code: SetTheory.PGame.lf_iff_lt_or_fuzzy.{u_1} {x y : PGame} : x ⧏ y ↔ x < y ∨ x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.lf_iff_lt_or_fuzzy.description: This theorem states that one game is strictly less than another if and only if it is either less than the second game or is fuzzy compared to it.

SetTheory.PGame.lf_of_fuzzy.code: SetTheory.PGame.lf_of_fuzzy.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ‖ y) : x ⧏ y
SetTheory.PGame.lf_of_fuzzy.description: This theorem establishes that if two game positions are fuzzy equivalent, then the first position is less than the second position in terms of game value.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.lf.code: SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.lf.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ‖ y) : x ⧏ y

explanatories.LT.lt.lf: This theorem states that if one pre-game is strictly less than another, it implies that the first pre-game is also strictly less than the second in the context of game relationships.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.lf.description: This theorem asserts that if two games are fuzzy equivalent, then the first game is strictly less than the second.

SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_fuzzy_of_lf.code: SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_fuzzy_of_lf.{u_1} {x y : PGame} : x ⧏ y → x < y ∨ x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_fuzzy_of_lf.description: This theorem states that if one game structure is less than another, it can either be strictly less than or fuzzy equal to that game.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv.code: SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ‖ y) : ¬x ≈ y

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.LF.not_equiv: This theorem asserts that if one game structure is strictly less than another, then these two game structures cannot be regarded as equivalent.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv.description: This theorem asserts that if two games are strictly fuzzy related, then they cannot be equivalent.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv'.code: SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv'.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ‖ y) : ¬y ≈ x

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.LF.not_equiv': This theorem establishes that if one game is strictly less than another, then the two games cannot be equivalent.

SetTheory.PGame.Fuzzy.not_equiv'.description: This theorem asserts that if two game positions are fuzzy equivalent, then the second position cannot be considered equivalent to the first position.

SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_le.code: SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_le.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ≤ y) : ¬x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_le.description: This theorem states that if one game is less than or equal to another, then they cannot be indistinguishable in terms of their strategic outcomes.

SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_ge.code: SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_ge.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : y ≤ x) : ¬x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.not_fuzzy_of_ge.description: This theorem states that if one game position is less than or equal to another, then those two positions cannot be considered indistinguishable in terms of their strategic merits.

SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy.code: SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ≈ y) : ¬x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy.description: This theorem asserts that if two games are equivalent, then they cannot be indistinctly presented as fuzzy or indistinguishable.

SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy'.code: SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy'.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (h : x ≈ y) : ¬y ‖ x
SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.not_fuzzy'.description: This theorem states that if two game positions are equivalent, then they cannot be considered indistinguishable in terms of their strategic qualities.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr.{u_1} {x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ : PGame} (hx : x₁ ≈ x₂) (hy : y₁ ≈ y₂) : x₁ ‖ y₁ ↔ x₂ ‖ y₂
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr.description: This theorem expresses that if two pairs of games are fuzzy equivalent, then their respective fuzzy comparisons yield the same truth value.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_imp.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_imp.{u_1} {x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ : PGame} (hx : x₁ ≈ x₂) (hy : y₁ ≈ y₂) : x₁ ‖ y₁ → x₂ ‖ y₂
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_imp.description: This theorem states that if two pairs of game positions are equivalent respectively, then the indistinguishability between the first pair implies indistinguishability between the second pair.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_left.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_left.{u_1} {x₁ x₂ y : PGame} (hx : x₁ ≈ x₂) : x₁ ‖ y ↔ x₂ ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_left.description: This theorem establishes that if two pre-games are equivalent, then the combination of either with a third pre-game yields equivalent results.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_right.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_right.{u_1} {x y₁ y₂ : PGame} (hy : y₁ ≈ y₂) : x ‖ y₁ ↔ x ‖ y₂
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_congr_right.description: This theorem shows that if two game structures are equivalent, then a given relationship with one of them holds if and only if it holds with the other.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_fuzzy_of_equiv.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_fuzzy_of_equiv.{u_1} {x y z : PGame} (h₁ : x ‖ y) (h₂ : y ≈ z) : x ‖ z
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_fuzzy_of_equiv.description: This theorem establishes that if one game is fuzzy related to another and that second game is equivalent to a third, then the first game is also fuzzy related to the third game.

SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_equiv_of_fuzzy.code: SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_equiv_of_fuzzy.{u_1} {x y z : PGame} (h₁ : x ≈ y) (h₂ : y ‖ z) : x ‖ z
SetTheory.PGame.fuzzy_of_equiv_of_fuzzy.description: This theorem asserts that if two games are equivalent and one of them is fuzzy with respect to a third game, then the first game is also fuzzy with respect to that third game.

SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gt_or_fuz.code: SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gt_or_fuzzy.{u_1} (x y : PGame) : x < y ∨ x ≈ y ∨ y < x ∨ x ‖ y
SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gt_or_fuz.comment: Exactly one of the following is true (although we don't prove this here).
SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gt_or_fuz.description: This theorem asserts that for any two games, exactly one of the following relationships holds: the first game is less than the second, they are equivalent, the second game is less than the first, or they are incomparable.

SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gf.code: SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gf.{u_1} (x y : PGame) : x < y ∨ x ≈ y ∨ y ⧏ x
SetTheory.PGame.lt_or_equiv_or_gf.description: For any two positions in a game, at least one of the following holds: the first position is less than the second, they are equivalent, or the second position is preferable to the first.

SetTheory.PGame.relabelRelabelling.fullDefinition: def relabelRelabelling {x : PGame} {xl' xr'} (el : xl' ≃ x.LeftMoves) (er : xr' ≃ x.RightMoves) :     x ≡r relabel el er :=   -- Porting note: needed to add `rfl`   Relabelling.mk' el er (fun i => by simp; rfl) (fun j => by simp; rfl)
SetTheory.PGame.relabelRelabelling.description: This definition states that when the moves of a game are relabelled according to two isomorphisms, the modified game is equivalent to the original game under that relabelling.

SetTheory.PGame.neg.description: This definition introduces the negation of a game, which switches the roles of the players, effectively transforming a position where one player can win to one where that player's opponent can win instead.

SetTheory.PGame.neg_def.code:

  -mk xl xr xL xR = mk xr xl (fun j => -xR j) fun i => -xL i

SetTheory.PGame.Relabelling.addCongr.fullDefinition: def Relabelling.addCongr : ∀ {w x y z : PGame.{u}}, w ≡r x → y ≡r z → w + y ≡r x + z   | ⟨wl, wr, wL, wR⟩, ⟨xl, xr, xL, xR⟩, ⟨yl, yr, yL, yR⟩, ⟨zl, zr, zL, zR⟩, ⟨L₁, R₁, hL₁, hR₁⟩,     ⟨L₂, R₂, hL₂, hR₂⟩ => by     let Hwx : ⟨wl, wr, wL, wR⟩ ≡r ⟨xl, xr, xL, xR⟩ := ⟨L₁, R₁, hL₁, hR₁⟩     let Hyz : ⟨yl, yr, yL, yR⟩ ≡r ⟨zl, zr, zL, zR⟩ := ⟨L₂, R₂, hL₂, hR₂⟩     refine ⟨Equiv.sumCongr L₁ L₂, Equiv.sumCongr R₁ R₂, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> rintro (i | j)     · exact (hL₁ i).addCongr Hyz     · exact Hwx.addCongr (hL₂ j)     · exact (hR₁ i).addCongr Hyz     · exact Hwx.addCongr (hR₂ j) termination_by _ x _ z => (x, z)

SetTheory.Game.comment:
The type of combinatorial games. In ZFC, a combinatorial game is constructed from
two sets of combinatorial games that have been constructed at an earlier
stage. To do this in type theory, we say that a combinatorial pre-game is built
inductively from two families of combinatorial games indexed over any type
in Type u. The resulting type `PGame.{u}` lives in `Type (u+1)`,
reflecting that it is a proper class in ZFC.
A combinatorial game is then constructed by quotienting by the equivalence
`x ≈ y ↔ x ≤ y ∧ y ≤ x`.

explanatories.Quotient: The quotient of a set using an equivalence relation is a type that represents the distinct equivalence classes formed by that relation.

SetTheory.Game.description: This definition describes the type of combinatorial games as being constructed inductively from pairs of earlier games and classified in a way that allows for their comparison and equivalence within type theory.

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.lf_congr: This theorem establishes that if two pairs of games are equivalent, then the first game in each pair is strictly preferred over the second game in the first pair if and only if the corresponding games in the second pair are also strictly preferred.

SetTheory.Game.LF.fullDefinition: def LF : Game → Game → Prop :=   Quotient.lift₂ PGame.LF fun _ _ _ _ hx hy => propext (lf_congr hx hy)
SetTheory.Game.LF.description: This definition establishes a relation on combinatorial games that indicates if the first player can win by playing optimally.

SetTheory.Game.instAddCommGroupWithOneGa.fullDefinition: instance instAddCommGroupWithOneGame : AddCommGroupWithOne Game where   zero := ⟦0⟧   one := ⟦1⟧   add_zero := by     rintro ⟨x⟩     exact Quot.sound (add_zero_equiv x)   zero_add := by     rintro ⟨x⟩     exact Quot.sound (zero_add_equiv x)   add_assoc := by     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩ ⟨z⟩     exact Quot.sound add_assoc_equiv   add_left_neg := Quotient.ind <| fun x => Quot.sound (add_left_neg_equiv x)   add_comm := by     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩     exact Quot.sound add_comm_equiv   nsmul := nsmulRec   zsmul := zsmulRec

SetTheory.Game.instPartialOrderGame.fullDefinition: instance instPartialOrderGame : PartialOrder Game where   le := Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ ·) fun x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ hx hy => propext (le_congr hx hy)   le_refl := by     rintro ⟨x⟩     exact le_refl x   le_trans := by     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩ ⟨z⟩     exact @le_trans _ _ x y z   le_antisymm := by     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩ h₁ h₂     apply Quot.sound     exact ⟨h₁, h₂⟩   lt := Quotient.lift₂ (· < ·) fun x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ hx hy => propext (lt_congr hx hy)   lt_iff_le_not_le := by     rintro ⟨x⟩ ⟨y⟩     exact @lt_iff_le_not_le _ _ x y

explanatories.Equiv.sumCongr: This definition asserts that the sum of two equivalences between types results in an equivalence between the sums of those types.
explanatories.Equiv.prodComm: This definition states that the product of two types is commutative up to an equivalence, asserting that the pairing of two types is equivalent to the pairing in the reverse order.

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.Relabelling.subCongr: This definition asserts that if two games are equivalent through relabelling and another pair of games is also equivalent through relabelling, then the difference of the first pair of games is equivalent to the difference of the second pair through relabelling as well.

SetTheory.PGame.mulCommRelabelling.fullDefinition: def mulCommRelabelling (x y : PGame.{u}) : x * y ≡r y * x :=   match x, y with   | ⟨xl, xr, xL, xR⟩, ⟨yl, yr, yL, yR⟩ => by     refine ⟨Equiv.sumCongr (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (Equiv.prodComm _ _),       (Equiv.sumComm _ _).trans (Equiv.sumCongr (Equiv.prodComm _ _) (Equiv.prodComm _ _)), ?_, ?_⟩       <;>     rintro (⟨i, j⟩ | ⟨i, j⟩) <;>     { dsimp       exact ((addCommRelabelling _ _).trans <|         (mulCommRelabelling _ _).addCongr (mulCommRelabelling _ _)).subCongr         (mulCommRelabelling _ _) }   termination_by (x, y)

SetTheory.PGame.negMulRelabelling.fullDefinition: def negMulRelabelling (x y : PGame.{u}) : -x * y ≡r -(x * y) :=   match x, y with   | ⟨xl, xr, xL, xR⟩, ⟨yl, yr, yL, yR⟩ => by       refine ⟨Equiv.sumComm _ _, Equiv.sumComm _ _, ?_, ?_⟩ <;>       rintro (⟨i, j⟩ | ⟨i, j⟩) <;>       · dsimp         apply ((negAddRelabelling _ _).trans _).symm         apply ((negAddRelabelling _ _).trans (Relabelling.addCongr _ _)).subCongr         -- Porting note: we used to just do `<;> exact (negMulRelabelling _ _).symm` from here.         · exact (negMulRelabelling _ _).symm         · exact (negMulRelabelling _ _).symm         -- Porting note: not sure what has gone wrong here.         -- The goal is hideous here, and the `exact` doesn't work,         -- but if we just `change` it to look like the mathlib3 goal then we're fine!?         change -(mk xl xr xL xR * _) ≡r _         exact (negMulRelabelling _ _).symm   termination_by (x, y)

SetTheory.PGame.mulOneRelabelling.fullDefinition: def mulOneRelabelling : ∀ x : PGame.{u}, x * 1 ≡r x   | ⟨xl, xr, xL, xR⟩ => by     -- Porting note: the next four lines were just `unfold has_one.one,`     show _ * One.one ≡r _     unfold One.one     unfold instOnePGame     change mk _ _ _ _ * mk _ _ _ _ ≡r _     refine ⟨(Equiv.sumEmpty _ _).trans (Equiv.prodPUnit _),       (Equiv.emptySum _ _).trans (Equiv.prodPUnit _), ?_, ?_⟩ <;>     (try rintro (⟨i, ⟨⟩⟩ | ⟨i, ⟨⟩⟩)) <;>     { dsimp       apply (Relabelling.subCongr (Relabelling.refl _) (mulZeroRelabelling _)).trans       rw [sub_zero]       exact (addZeroRelabelling _).trans <|         (((mulOneRelabelling _).addCongr (mulZeroRelabelling _)).trans <| addZeroRelabelling _) }

SetTheory.PGame.invVal.fullDefinition: def invVal {l r} (L : l → PGame) (R : r → PGame) (IHl : l → PGame) (IHr : r → PGame)     (x : PGame) : ∀ {b}, InvTy l r b → PGame   | _, InvTy.zero => 0   | _, InvTy.left₁ i j => (1 + (R i - x) * invVal L R IHl IHr x j) * IHr i   | _, InvTy.left₂ i j => (1 + (L i - x) * invVal L R IHl IHr x j) * IHl i   | _, InvTy.right₁ i j => (1 + (L i - x) * invVal L R IHl IHr x j) * IHl i   | _, InvTy.right₂ i j => (1 + (R i - x) * invVal L R IHl IHr x j) * IHr i
SetTheory.PGame.invVal.description: This definition specifies a recursive function that constructs a combinatorial game from an inverse type by using two families of games corresponding to each part of the inverse structure.

SetTheory.PGame.inv'.comment:
The inverse of a positive surreal number `x = {L | R}` is
given by `x⁻¹ = {0,
  (1 + (R - x) * x⁻¹L) * R, (1 + (L - x) * x⁻¹R) * L |
  (1 + (L - x) * x⁻¹L) * L, (1 + (R - x) * x⁻¹R) * R}`.
Because the two halves `x⁻¹L, x⁻¹R` of `x⁻¹` are used in their own
definition, the sets and elements are inductively generated.

SetTheory.PGame.inv'.fullDefinition: def inv' : PGame → PGame   | ⟨l, r, L, R⟩ =>     let l' := { i // 0 < L i }     let L' : l' → PGame := fun i => L i.1     let IHl' : l' → PGame := fun i => inv' (L i.1)     let IHr i := inv' (R i)     let x := mk l r L R     ⟨InvTy l' r false, InvTy l' r true, invVal L' R IHl' IHr x, invVal L' R IHl' IHr x⟩

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.Equiv.trans: This theorem establishes that the equivalence relation for pre-games is transitive, meaning if one pre-game is equivalent to a second, and that second is equivalent to a third, then the first and third must also be equivalent.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.Relabelling.symm: This definition establishes that if one pre-game is related to another through a relabelling, then the reverse relationship also holds, flipping the relabelling.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.Relabelling.equiv: This theorem establishes that if two games are related by a relabelling equivalence, they are also considered equivalent in terms of game outcomes.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.add_congr: This theorem asserts that if two games are equivalent respectively and another pair of games is also equivalent, then the sum of the first pair of games is equivalent to the sum of the second pair.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.negAddRelabelling: This definition states that the negated sum of two games has the same structure as the sum of their individual negations, meaning they can be relabeled equivalently to reflect the same possible moves.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.leftMoves_add_cases: This theorem states that if a property holds for all left moves arising from two games combined, then it also holds for any specific left move in that combined game.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.add_moveLeft_inl: This theorem shows that making a left move in the sum of two games results in the same outcome as making a left move in the first game and then adding the second game.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.add_moveLeft_inr: This theorem asserts that performing a left move in the sum of two game positions is equivalent to moving left in the second game while preserving the addition with the first game.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.rightMoves_add_cases: This theorem states that for any right move in the sum of two games, if a property holds for each right move of the individual games, then it also holds for the right move in their sum.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.add_moveRight_inl: This theorem demonstrates that making a right move in the sum of two games corresponds to making a right move in the first game and maintaining the second game unchanged.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.add_moveRight_inr: This theorem demonstrates that making a right move in a sum of two game structures gives the same outcome as maintaining the first game and making a right move in the second game.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.

SetTheory.PGame.Impartial.impartial_add.fullDefinition: instance impartial_add : ∀ (G H : PGame) [G.Impartial] [H.Impartial], (G + H).Impartial   | G, H, _, _ => by     rw [impartial_def]     refine ⟨Equiv.trans (add_congr (neg_equiv_self G) (neg_equiv_self _))         (Equiv.symm (negAddRelabelling _ _).equiv), fun k => ?_, fun k => ?_⟩     · apply leftMoves_add_cases k       all_goals         intro i; simp only [add_moveLeft_inl, add_moveLeft_inr]         apply impartial_add     · apply rightMoves_add_cases k       all_goals         intro i; simp only [add_moveRight_inl, add_moveRight_inr]         apply impartial_add termination_by G H => (G, H)

explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.State.turnBound: This definition introduces a function that assigns a natural number to each state in a game, representing a bound related to the game's progression.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.turnBound_ne_zero_of_lef: This theorem asserts that if a left move from a state to another state exists in a game, then the bound of the original state must be non-zero.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.turnBound_of_left: This theorem establishes that if a left move exists from one state to another in a game and the bound of the original state does not exceed a certain value, then the bound of the resulting state is also limited to that value.
explanatories.nonpos_iff_eq_zero: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, an element is less than or equal to zero if and only if it is equal to zero.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.SetTheory.PGame.LeftMoves: This definition specifies the type of permissible moves that a player designated as "Left" can make within a game structure.
explanatories.Nat.le_trans: This theorem establishes that if one number is less than or equal to a second number, and that second number is less than or equal to a third number, then the first number is also less than or equal to the third number.
explanatories.le_tsub_add: This theorem states that any element is less than or equal to its difference from another element plus that other element.

SetTheory.PGame.relabellingMoveLeftAux.description: This definition demonstrates that applying a left move to a game created from a specific state and bound results in a game that can be represented as another state created from a modified bound and a corresponding state reachable through left moves.

SetTheory.PGame.shortOfStateAux.fullDefinition: instance shortOfStateAux : ∀ (n : ℕ) {s : S} (h : turnBound s ≤ n), Short (ofStateAux n s h)   | 0, s, h =>     Short.mk'       (fun i => by         have i := (leftMovesOfStateAux _ _).toFun i         exfalso         exact turnBound_ne_zero_of_left_move i.2 (nonpos_iff_eq_zero.mp h))       fun j => by       have j := (rightMovesOfStateAux _ _).toFun j       exfalso       exact turnBound_ne_zero_of_right_move j.2 (nonpos_iff_eq_zero.mp h)   | n + 1, s, h =>     Short.mk'       (fun i =>         shortOfRelabelling (relabellingMoveLeftAux (n + 1) h i).symm (shortOfStateAux n _))       fun j =>       shortOfRelabelling (relabellingMoveRightAux (n + 1) h j).symm (shortOfStateAux n _)
SetTheory.PGame.shortOfStateAux.description: This definition asserts that a game represented with a specific state and turn bound is considered "short" if the turn bound of that state does not exceed a given natural number.

Ordinal.add_covariantClass_le.fullDefinition: instance add_covariantClass_le : CovariantClass Ordinal.{u} Ordinal.{u} (· + ·) (· ≤ ·) where   elim := fun c a b h => by     revert h c     refine inductionOn a (fun α₁ r₁ _ ↦ ?_)     refine inductionOn b (fun α₂ r₂ _ ↦ ?_)     rintro c ⟨⟨⟨f, fo⟩, fi⟩⟩     refine inductionOn c (fun β s _ ↦ ?_)     refine ⟨⟨⟨(Embedding.refl.{u+1} _).sumMap f, ?_⟩, ?_⟩⟩     · intros a b       match a, b with       | Sum.inl a, Sum.inl b => exact Sum.lex_inl_inl.trans Sum.lex_inl_inl.symm       | Sum.inl a, Sum.inr b => apply iff_of_true <;> apply Sum.Lex.sep       | Sum.inr a, Sum.inl b => apply iff_of_false <;> exact Sum.lex_inr_inl       | Sum.inr a, Sum.inr b => exact Sum.lex_inr_inr.trans <| fo.trans Sum.lex_inr_inr.symm     · intros a b H       match a, b, H with       | _, Sum.inl b, _ => exact ⟨Sum.inl b, rfl⟩       | Sum.inl a, Sum.inr b, H => exact (Sum.lex_inr_inl H).elim       | Sum.inr a, Sum.inr b, H =>         let ⟨w, h⟩ := fi _ _ (Sum.lex_inr_inr.1 H)         exact ⟨Sum.inr w, congr_arg Sum.inr h⟩

Ordinal.lift.principalSeg.fullDefinition: def lift.principalSeg : @PrincipalSeg Ordinal.{u} Ordinal.{max (u + 1) v} (· < ·) (· < ·) :=   ⟨↑lift.initialSeg.{u, max (u + 1) v}, univ.{u, v}, by     refine fun b => inductionOn b ?_; intro β s _     rw [univ, ← lift_umax]; constructor <;> intro h     · rw [← lift_id (type s)] at h ⊢       cases' lift_type_lt.{_,_,v}.1 h with f       cases' f with f a hf       exists a       revert hf       -- Porting note: apply inductionOn does not work, refine does       refine inductionOn a ?_       intro α r _ hf       refine         lift_type_eq.{u, max (u + 1) v, max (u + 1) v}.2           ⟨(RelIso.ofSurjective (RelEmbedding.ofMonotone ?_ ?_) ?_).symm⟩       · exact fun b => enum r (f b) ((hf _).2 ⟨_, rfl⟩)       · refine fun a b h => (typein_lt_typein r).1 ?_         rw [typein_enum, typein_enum]         exact f.map_rel_iff.2 h       · intro a'         cases' (hf _).1 (typein_lt_type _ a') with b e         exists b         simp only [RelEmbedding.ofMonotone_coe]         simp [e]     · cases' h with a e       rw [← e]       refine inductionOn a ?_       intro α r _       exact lift_type_lt.{u, u + 1, max (u + 1) v}.2 ⟨typein.principalSeg r⟩⟩

explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.RelIso.trans: The composition of two relation isomorphisms results in another relation isomorphism.

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.
explanatories.InitialSeg.trans_apply: This theorem establishes that if two initial segment order embeddings are composed, the result when applied to an element is equal to applying the second embedding to the result of the first embedding on that element, illustrating how the embeddings interact.
explanatories.InitialSeg.leAdd_apply: This theorem asserts that applying the initial segment embedding from one ordered set to a specific element results in the left injection of that element into the disjoint union of two ordered sets.
explanatories.InitialSeg.eq: This theorem asserts that two order embeddings defined by an initial segment are equal on a given element if the target set is well-ordered.
explanatories.InitialSeg.leAdd: This definition establishes an initial segment embedding of an ordered set into the lexicographic order of the disjoint union of two ordered sets.
explanatories.InitialSeg.trans: This definition asserts that if there are two initial segment order embeddings, the composition of these embeddings also results in an initial segment order embedding, illustrating the transitive nature of this relation.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection into the sum type combines an element from one type with the sum type, indicating it originates from the second type.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.inj': An embedding is proven to be an injective function.
explanatories.InitialSeg.coe_coe_fn: This theorem asserts that the action of an order embedding with the initial segment property is equal to its corresponding relational embedding function.
explanatories.Function.Embedding.coeFn_mk: The concept of an equivalence allows for the translation of elements between sets while maintaining their structural properties.
explanatories.RelEmbedding.map_rel_iff: A theorem stating that the application of a well-founded relation to an element demonstrates its accessibility within that relation.
explanatories.InitialSeg.toRelEmbedding: This definition specifies a method to convert an order embedding with an initial segment property into a relational embedding between two partially ordered sets.
explanatories.InitialSeg.init: This theorem states that if an element in the target partially ordered set is less than the image of an element in the source set under an initial segment embedding, then there exists a preimage in the source set that maps to that target element.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Sum.inr.inj: If two values are represented as the right component in a sum type, then they are equal if the representations are equal.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Iff.trans: If two propositions are each equivalent to a third proposition, then they are equivalent to each other.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Or.inl: If a proposition is true, then it can be included in a disjunction, demonstrating how to inject it into the logical framework of 'or'.
explanatories.Or.inr: If there is a proof of a proposition, it can be included in a disjunction as the second option.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.WellOrder.α: This definition describes the underlying type associated with a well-ordering.
explanatories.Quotient.inductionOn: For any property defined on a quotient type, if that property holds for representatives of each equivalence class, it holds for the entire quotient.
explanatories.Cardinal.mk: This defines a function that assigns a cardinal number to a type, representing the size of that type.
explanatories.Quotient.mk: The canonical quotient map transforms an element into its associated equivalence class under a given setoid.
explanatories.Subtype.eq: If two elements of a subtype have the same underlying value, then they are considered equal as elements of that subtype.
explanatories.Acc.intro: A value is considered accessible if all related values are also accessible under a given relation, establishing a basis for cases with no related values.

Ordinal.add_contravariantClass_le.fullDefinition: instance add_contravariantClass_le : ContravariantClass Ordinal.{u} Ordinal.{u} (· + ·) (· ≤ ·) :=   ⟨fun a b c =>     inductionOn a fun α r hr =>       inductionOn b fun β₁ s₁ hs₁ =>         inductionOn c fun β₂ s₂ hs₂ ⟨f⟩ =>           ⟨have fl : ∀ a, f (Sum.inl a) = Sum.inl a := fun a => by               simpa only [InitialSeg.trans_apply, InitialSeg.leAdd_apply] using                 @InitialSeg.eq _ _ _ _ _                   ((InitialSeg.leAdd r s₁).trans f) (InitialSeg.leAdd r s₂) a             have : ∀ b, { b' // f (Sum.inr b) = Sum.inr b' } := by               intro b; cases e : f (Sum.inr b)               · rw [← fl] at e                 have := f.inj' e                 contradiction               · exact ⟨_, rfl⟩             let g (b) := (this b).1             have fr : ∀ b, f (Sum.inr b) = Sum.inr (g b) := fun b => (this b).2             ⟨⟨⟨g, fun x y h => by                   injection f.inj' (by rw [fr, fr, h] : f (Sum.inr x) = f (Sum.inr y))⟩,                 @fun a b => by                   -- Porting note:                   --  `relEmbedding.coe_fn_to_embedding` & `initial_seg.coe_fn_to_rel_embedding`                   --  → `InitialSeg.coe_coe_fn`                   simpa only [Sum.lex_inr_inr, fr, InitialSeg.coe_coe_fn, Embedding.coeFn_mk] using                     @RelEmbedding.map_rel_iff _ _ _ _ f.toRelEmbedding (Sum.inr a) (Sum.inr b)⟩,               fun a b H => by                 rcases f.init (by rw [fr] <;> exact Sum.lex_inr_inr.2 H) with ⟨a' | a', h⟩                 · rw [fl] at h                   cases h                 · rw [fr] at h                   exact ⟨a', Sum.inr.inj h⟩⟩⟩⟩
Ordinal.add_contravariantClass_le.description: This definition establishes a contravariant relationship between the addition of ordinals and the ordering of ordinals.

Ordinal.nadd.comment:
Natural addition on ordinals `a ♯ b`, also known as the Hessenberg sum, is recursively defined
as the least ordinal greater than `a' ♯ b` and `a ♯ b'` for all `a' < a` and `b' < b`. In contrast
to normal ordinal addition, it is commutative.

Natural addition can equivalently be characterized as the ordinal resulting from adding up
corresponding coefficients in the Cantor normal forms of `a` and `b`.

explanatories.Max.max: A function computes the maximum of two elements from a specified type.

Ordinal.nmul.comment:
Natural multiplication on ordinals `a ⨳ b`, also known as the Hessenberg product, is recursively
defined as the least ordinal such that `a ⨳ b + a' ⨳ b'` is greater than `a' ⨳ b + a ⨳ b'` for all
`a' < a` and `b < b'`. In contrast to normal ordinal multiplication, it is commutative and
distributive (over natural addition).

Natural multiplication can equivalently be characterized as the ordinal resulting from multiplying
the Cantor normal forms of `a` and `b` as if they were polynomials in `ω`. Addition of exponents is
done via natural addition.

Ordinal.nmul.description: This definition introduces a natural multiplication operation on ordinals that behaves commutatively and distributively.

Ordinal.nfpFamily.comment:
The next common fixed point, at least `a`, for a family of normal functions.

This is defined for any family of functions, as the supremum of all values reachable by applying
finitely many functions in the family to `a`.

`Ordinal.nfpFamily_fp` shows this is a fixed point, `Ordinal.le_nfpFamily` shows it's at
least `a`, and `Ordinal.nfpFamily_le_fp` shows this is the least ordinal with these properties.

explanatories.Ordinal.IsNormal.sup: This theorem asserts that if a function is normal, then the image of the supremum of a set under that function equals the supremum of the images of the elements of that set.

Ordinal.derivFamily.comment:

Ordinal.Principal.comment:
An ordinal `o` is said to be principal or indecomposable under an operation when the set of
ordinals less than it is closed under that operation. In standard mathematical usage, this term is
almost exclusively used for additive and multiplicative principal ordinals.

For simplicity, we break usual convention and regard 0 as principal.

ONote.fundamentalSequence.eq_2 (e : ONote) (n : ℕ+) (a : ONote) :
  (e.oadd n a).fundamentalSequence =
    match a.fundamentalSequence with
    | Sum.inr f => Sum.inr fun i => e.oadd n (f i)
    | Sum.inl (some b') => Sum.inl (some (e.oadd n b'))
    | Sum.inl none =>
      match e.fundamentalSequence, n.natPred with
      | Sum.inl none, 0 => Sum.inl (some zero)
      | Sum.inl none, m.succ => Sum.inl (some (zero.oadd m.succPNat zero))
      | Sum.inl (some a'), 0 => Sum.inr fun i => a'.oadd i.succPNat zero
      | Sum.inl (some a'), m.succ => Sum.inr fun i => e.oadd m.succPNat (a'.oadd i.succPNat zero)
      | Sum.inr f, 0 => Sum.inr fun i => (f i).oadd 1 zero
      | Sum.inr f, m.succ => Sum.inr fun i => e.oadd m.succPNat ((f i).oadd 1 zero)

ONote.fastGrowing.comment:
The fast growing hierarchy for ordinal notations `< ε₀`. This is a sequence of
functions `ℕ → ℕ` indexed by ordinals, with the definition:
* `f_0(n) = n + 1`
* `f_(α+1)(n) = f_α^[n](n)`
* `f_α(n) = f_(α[n])(n)` where `α` is a limit ordinal
   and `α[i]` is the fundamental sequence converging to `α`

onote.fast_growing.comment:
The fast growing hierarchy for ordinal notations `< ε₀`. This is a sequence of
functions `ℕ → ℕ` indexed by ordinals, with the definition:
* `f_0(n) = n + 1`
* `f_(α+1)(n) = f_α^[n](n)`
* `f_α(n) = f_(α[n])(n)` where `α` is a limit ordinal
   and `α[i]` is the fundamental sequence converging to `α`

    x.fastGrowing =
      match (motive := (x_1 : Option ONote ⊕ (ℕ → ONote)) → x.FundamentalSequenceProp x_1 → ℕ → ℕ)
        x.fundamentalSequence, ⋯ with
      | Sum.inl none, x => Nat.succ
      | Sum.inl (some a), h =>
        let_fun this := ⋯;
        fun i => a.fastGrowing^[i] i
      | Sum.inr f, h => fun i =>
        let_fun this := ⋯;
        (f i).fastGrowing i

SetTheory.PGame.lt_def.code:
SetTheory.PGame.lt_def.{u_1} {x y : PGame} (ox : x.Numeric) (oy : y.Numeric) :
  x < y ↔
    (∃ i,
        (∀ (i' : x.LeftMoves), x.moveLeft i' < y.moveLeft i) ∧
          ∀ (j : (y.moveLeft i).RightMoves), x < (y.moveLeft i).moveRight j) ∨
      ∃ j,
        (∀ (i : (x.moveRight j).LeftMoves), (x.moveRight j).moveLeft i < y) ∧
          ∀ (j' : y.RightMoves), x.moveRight j < y.moveRight j'

Surreal.Multiplication.P3.comment: The proposition P3, without the `x₁ < x₂` and `y₁ < y₂` assumptions.
Surreal.Multiplication.P3.fullDefinition: def P3 (x₁ x₂ y₁ y₂ : PGame) := ⟦x₁ * y₂⟧ + ⟦x₂ * y₁⟧ < ⟦x₁ * y₁⟧ + (⟦x₂ * y₂⟧ : Game)
Surreal.Multiplication.P3.description: This definition outlines a proposition related to the multiplication of two pre-game structures without imposing any ordering constraints on their components.

Surreal.Multiplication.P2.comment: The proposition P2, without numericity assumptions.
Surreal.Multiplication.P2.fullDefinition: def P2 (x₁ x₂ y : PGame) := x₁ ≈ x₂ → ⟦x₁ * y⟧ = (⟦x₂ * y⟧ : Game)
Surreal.Multiplication.P2.description: This definition introduces a proposition regarding the multiplication of pre-game structures without assuming any numerical properties.

Surreal.Multiplication.P4.comment:
The proposition P4, without numericity assumptions. In the references, the second part of the
conjunction is stated as `∀ j, P3 x₁ x₂ y (y.moveRight j)`, which is equivalent to our statement
by `P3_comm` and `P3_neg`. We choose to state everything in terms of left options for uniform
treatment.

Surreal.Multiplication.P1.comment:
The nontrivial part of P1 in [SchleicherStoll] says that the left options of `x * y`
are less than the right options, and this is the general form of these statements.
Surreal.Multiplication.P1.fullDefinition: def P1 (x₁ x₂ x₃ y₁ y₂ y₃ : PGame) :=   ⟦x₁ * y₁⟧ + ⟦x₂ * y₂⟧ - ⟦x₁ * y₂⟧ < ⟦x₃ * y₁⟧ + ⟦x₂ * y₃⟧ - (⟦x₃ * y₃⟧ : Game)
Surreal.Multiplication.P1.description: This definition outlines a proposition concerning the ordering of left and right options in the multiplication of pre-game structures, indicating that the left options are lesser than the right options.

Surreal.Multiplication.IH3.code: Surreal.Multiplication.IH3.{u_1} (x₁ x' x₂ y₁ y₂ : PGame) : Prop
Surreal.Multiplication.IH3.comment:
A condition just enough to deduce P3, which will always be used with `x'` being a left
option of `x₂`. When `y₁` is a left option of `y₂`, it can be deduced from induction hypotheses
`IH24 x₁ x₂ y₂`, `IH4 x₁ x₂ y₂`, and `(x₂ * y₂).Numeric` (`ih3_of_ih`); when `y₁` is
not necessarily an option of `y₂`, it follows from the induction hypothesis for P3 (with `x₂`
replaced by a left option `x'`) after the `main` theorem (P124) is established, and is used to
prove P3 in full (`P3_of_lt_of_lt`).

SetTheory.PGame.powHalf.comment:
For a natural number `n`, the pre-game `powHalf (n + 1)` is recursively defined as
`{0 | powHalf n}`. These are the explicit expressions of powers of `1 / 2`. By definition, we have
`powHalf 0 = 1` and `powHalf 1 ≈ 1 / 2` and we prove later on that
`powHalf (n + 1) + powHalf (n + 1) ≈ powHalf n`.
SetTheory.PGame.powHalf.fullDefinition: def powHalf : ℕ → PGame   | 0 => 1   | n + 1 => ⟨PUnit, PUnit, 0, fun _ => powHalf n⟩
SetTheory.PGame.powHalf.description: This definition constructs a family of pre-game structures corresponding to powers of one-half, defined recursively based on natural numbers.

explanatories.Submonoid.log: The logarithm function maps powers of an element in a monoid to their corresponding natural number exponents.

explanatories.mul_eq_mul_left_iff: This theorem states that in a cancelable monoid with zero, the equality of two products implies either the factors are equal when the first factor is non-zero or the first factor is zero.
explanatories.Subtype.prop: This theorem asserts that for a specific subtype, the property defining the subtype holds when applied to its element.
explanatories.Submonoid.pow: The exponentiation map assigns natural numbers to the powers of a given element in a monoid.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.Int.natAbs: This defines a function that returns the absolute value of an integer as a natural number.
explanatories.one_lt_two: This theorem demonstrates that in any partially ordered additive monoid containing one and zero, one is less than two.
explanatories.Submonoid.log_pow_int_eq_self: For any integer greater than one, the logarithm of its power equals the exponent in the power.
explanatories.Localization.liftOn_zero: This theorem states that when lifting a function defined on a commutative monoid with zero, the value at the zero element can be expressed in terms of the function evaluated at zero and the identity element of the submonoid.
explanatories.Int.cast_zero: This theorem states that the zero of the integers is equal to the zero in the context of an additive group.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, demonstrating that zero acts as a left absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.Localization.induction_on₂: This theorem asserts that if a binary property holds for pairs of elements formed from a monoid and a submonoid, then it must also hold for the corresponding localized elements, thus facilitating the comparison of elements in the localization.
explanatories.Submonoid.pow_apply: The function that raises an element of a monoid to a natural number exponent produces a pair consisting of the result and additional structure.

explanatories.Localization.liftOn_mk: This theorem establishes that the application of a function to a localized element can be directly computed by applying the same function to the corresponding representatives from the original monoid and submonoid, provided that the function respects the defined equivalence relation.
explanatories.Submonoid.log_mul: The logarithm of the product of two powers of a given element in a monoid equals the sum of their logarithms, provided the function that maps exponents to powers is injective.
explanatories.Int.pow_right_injective: This theorem asserts that for integers whose absolute value is greater than one, the function that raises them to any integer power is injective.

Surreal.dyadicMap.fullDefinition: noncomputable def dyadicMap : Localization.Away (2 : ℤ) →+ Surreal where   toFun x :=     (Localization.liftOn x fun x y => x * powHalf (Submonoid.log y)) <| by       intro m₁ m₂ n₁ n₂ h₁       obtain ⟨⟨n₃, y₃, hn₃⟩, h₂⟩ := Localization.r_iff_exists.mp h₁       simp only [Subtype.coe_mk, mul_eq_mul_left_iff] at h₂       cases h₂       · obtain ⟨a₁, ha₁⟩ := n₁.prop         obtain ⟨a₂, ha₂⟩ := n₂.prop         simp only at ha₁ ha₂ ⊢         have hn₁ : n₁ = Submonoid.pow 2 a₁ := Subtype.ext ha₁.symm         have hn₂ : n₂ = Submonoid.pow 2 a₂ := Subtype.ext ha₂.symm         have h₂ : 1 < (2 : ℤ).natAbs := one_lt_two         rw [hn₁, hn₂, Submonoid.log_pow_int_eq_self h₂, Submonoid.log_pow_int_eq_self h₂]         apply dyadic_aux         rwa [ha₁, ha₂, mul_comm, mul_comm m₂]       · have : (1 : ℤ) ≤ 2 ^ y₃ := mod_cast Nat.one_le_pow y₃ 2 Nat.succ_pos'         linarith   map_zero' := by simp_rw [Localization.liftOn_zero _ _, Int.cast_zero, zero_mul]   map_add' x y :=     Localization.induction_on₂ x y <| by       rintro ⟨a, ⟨b, ⟨b', rfl⟩⟩⟩ ⟨c, ⟨d, ⟨d', rfl⟩⟩⟩       have h₂ : 1 < (2 : ℤ).natAbs := one_lt_two       have hpow₂ := Submonoid.log_pow_int_eq_self h₂       simp_rw [Submonoid.pow_apply] at hpow₂       simp_rw [Localization.add_mk, Localization.liftOn_mk,         Submonoid.log_mul (Int.pow_right_injective h₂), hpow₂]       simp only [Int.cast_add, Int.cast_mul, Int.cast_pow, Int.cast_ofNat]       calc         (2 ^ b' * c + 2 ^ d' * a) * powHalf (b' + d') =             (c * 2 ^ b') * powHalf (b' + d') + (a * 2 ^ d') * powHalf (d' + b') := by           simp only [right_distrib, mul_comm, add_comm]         _ = c * powHalf d' + a * powHalf b' := by simp only [zsmul_pow_two_powHalf]         _ = a * powHalf b' + c * powHalf d' := add_comm _ _
